newsitem.title: USA: Harken Colombia test results positive.
newsitem.headline: Harken Colombia test results positive.

text.p: Harken Energy Corp said Wednesday initial production testing of the Torcaz 3 well has been completed with very positive results.

This well, located on Harken's 30,000 acre Rio Negro Prospect in the Middle Magdalena Basin of Colombia, contains 52 percent more pay than the Torcaz 2, thereby exceeding earlier independent engineering estimates, Harken said.
On initial tests the well produced at a rate of 643 barrels per day, the company said in a statement.
Production tests indicate the oil is sand free and that produced formation water is very low to almost non-existent.

A dual stage process consisting of enzymes to consume drilling polymers and acid to remove residual "bridging" agents was added to the completion procedure which should result in increasing production flow rates over the next few months, Harken said.

To enhance the restricted production flow rates that were encountered in the Torcaz 2 last year, the drilling and completion procedure was modified by the use of a specialty drill-in fluid with "bridging" agents, and use of chlorides matched to formation values. A wire wrapped screen, to provide a greater flow area, was installed in the Torcaz 3 well in place of the slotted liner utilized at Torcaz 2.
Harken said, "We are pleased with the increased net pay and the production test. We believe that this improved completion technique will result in increasing flow rates as the well cleans up.
The company said it plans to move the rig from the Torcaz 3 location back to the Torcaz 2 for remedial work using this modified completion process.
